key_insight: Integrating object-centric representations into Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) enables precise instance-level grounding, consistent object identity across interactions, and controllable region-level editing and generation in visual scenes.
problem_solved: LMMs often fail at fine-grained, object-level tasks: they misidentify instances, lose object identity across interactions, and cannot localize or modify designated regions with high precision. This work addresses those limits by combining object-centric vision with multimodal reasoning.
method: Augment LMM architecture with an object-centric module (e.g., slot/instance representations) that extracts explicit object-level tokens or masks from images.

Jointly train multimodal objectives spanning instance segmentation, referring-expression grounding, editing and conditional generation to align object tokens with language and visual manipulation operators.
Condition text-to-image and editing operations on object-level representations to enable precise localization, identity-preserving interactions, and controllable generation.
impact: Makes multimodal systems practical for tasks requiring precise object reasoning — e.g., interactive image editing, fine-grained VQA, robotics perception, and AR — by improving accuracy, controllability, and identity preservation at the object level.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing LMM + object-centric module: image -> object slots/masks -> multimodal encoder -> grounded outputs (segmentation, edits, generation).
Before/after image pairs illustrating precise, identity-preserving edits (select object by text, modify color/shape, keep other objects unchanged).
Instance segmentation overlays with consistent color-coded object IDs across multiple interaction steps to show identity tracking.
Small bar or radar chart summarizing improvements on object-level metrics (grounding accuracy, IoU for segmentation, edit fidelity) alongside qualitative examples.
paper_title: LMMs Meet Object-Centric Vision: Understanding, Segmentation, Editing and Generation
paper_authors: Yuqian Yuan, Wenqiao Zhang, Juekai Lin, Yu Zhong, Mingjian Gao
